newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - London Evening Standard - Nov 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - London Evening Standard - Nov 27.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
NO VOTES OF THANKS FOR KEN

In an NOP poll carried out for public affairs consultancy Political Context, Kenneth Clarke's pre-election budget appears to have gained little support for the Conservatives. Mr Clarke's buoyant claim that families will benefit from the budget was believed by 17 per cent. 8 out 10 believe the budget will make them worse off, or make no difference.
RATE FEARS SIMMER IN WAKE OF BUDGET
Dealers reacted to Kenneth Clarke's Budget nervously, fearing that next year's income tax cuts could stoke up consumer demand and lead to higher interest rates.

Yesterday's Budget announced reductions in the capital allowances on machinery and plant with a working life of over 25 years from 25 percent to 6 percent, a move which will hit water and electricity companies. The government will raise 325 million stg from these changes in 1998, and up to 675 million stg in 1999.

Greenpeace is lobbying for a halt to the development of new oilfields west of Shetland. Companies like BP and Shell RD.AX believe two of the most important of these fields have recoverable reserves of between 250 million and 500 million barrels each.
FEELGOOD RETURNS TO HONG KONG PROPERTY

Following a prolonged slump Hong Kong's prime office property sector is showing signs of improvement. Yesterday deals were being priced at hefty premiums with higher than average market rates. Last week Hysan Development bought the Entertainment building for 17,300 Hong Kong dollars.
BANKERS HANG UP ON RUSSIAN TELECOM DEAL

Russia seems to have turned its back on foreign investors a week after completing its first international bond issue since Tsarist times. This week a group of western banks decided to withdraw a mandate to float the State's telecoms holdings after it became clear that the deal had been altered to involve a Russian consortium.
